title: Difference as mercy
hookLine: a well-known saying calls scholarly difference a mercy

lines: THE SUN SINKS ON THE ROAD.
cards: An instruction goes out to a company of the Prophet's companions: none of you is to pray the afternoon prayer except at the settlement of Banu Qurayza. They set off, and the sun drops lower on the road.

If they keep walking, the prayer's time will pass. One group says: he meant hurry, not miss the prayer, and they pray on the road. Another says: he said there, and they pray only when they arrive, late.
Same words, two honest readings. In Sahih al-Bukhari, when the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, hears about it, he blames neither group. Today's word is what happened on that road.

teach.b: The word is ikhtilaf: difference, disagreement, the scholars going different ways.

teach.h: A SAYING WITH NO SOUND CHAIN.
teach.b: People repeat a saying: the difference of my community is a mercy. It's quoted as a hadith, and here honesty matters. Hadith scholars have said they found no reliable chain for it back to the Prophet.
The idea, though, is carried by other reports.
A saying attributed to the caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz has him say he would not have been glad if the companions had never differed, because their difference left room for those who came after.
And a story the biographies tell: a caliph wanted to make Imam Malik's book, al-Muwatta, the single law for every city. Malik declined.

The companions had spread to different cities, he said, each carrying what they knew, and people should be left with what had reached them. Think back to the road: the same words, honest readings, neither group blamed.
That's the picture of a mercy. Two schools can place the hands differently in prayer, and both be following their method faithfully. But this isn't difference about everything.
It lives inside a shared ground: the oneness of God, the prayer, the fast, the Qur'an.

And it's reached by method, the method of the last two weeks: shari'ah and fiqh, the Qur'an and sunnah, agreement, analogy, reason, the common good, custom, the five rulings, the wide permitted, striving, following.
That closes the foundations. Next, the schools themselves, one by one, beginning with the merchant of Kufa.

how: Muslims of different schools pray and fast according to their own school's rulings side by side in the same mosques, and scholars study the reasons behind each school's view in a field called the study of disagreement.

o: a split that means one side has left the faith
disagreement about core beliefs, like the oneness of God
difference among scholars, reached by honest method

games.q: you're on the road to Banu Qurayza. you were told to pray the afternoon prayer only there, and the sun is setting. what do you do?
o: pray on the road, reading the order as 'hurry'.
pray only on arrival, reading the order as 'there'.
either: both groups did, and neither was blamed.
games.why: one group prayed on the road, the other on arrival. the Prophet blamed neither. two honest readings of the same words.

practice: Bring to mind a way someone else practices that isn't yours: some Muslims pray with arms folded and others with arms at their sides, each following their school, or a family that keeps a holiday differently from yours.
Hold it without correcting it, and ask what honest reading might be behind it, like the two groups on the road. If you pray, you can pray for the one who differs from you.

wordCard.voice: Ikhtilaf. Difference among scholars, reached by honest method, held as a mercy. Today's word.
